questions.conclusion: Under fixed p,q,N example budget and WR sampling, uniform exact aliases change nominal pool size but not empirical input/label distribution, gradients, optimizer updates or trajectory law. Nominal alias count is not a sufficient explanation of SB-SN.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Increasing genuinely independent support or changing underlying distribution is not the same intervention. Existing three physical domains confound independent support, distribution, labels, difficulty and architecture interactions. No claim that true statistical sample size cannot matter. No PERM invariance claim.
questions.minimal_identifying_design: To identify independent support, obtain additional independent rows from the same domain population, prespecify disjoint sampling/subsampling sets with matched difficulty, p,q and exposure, and repeat matched SN/SB training across independent dataset draws. Exact aliases do not supply such rows.
questions.next_action: Report nominal-pool invariance separately from independent-support size. Do not equate small domains with difficult domains; complete V8 corruption and cell audit for their separate questions.
